I'd like to hear from transportation, IT, nursing, and family engagement before I sign off on the operating plan. Who would like to start?

transcript.text: Dr. Lee, I need to flag a critical IT issue. Our learning-management-system authentication will be offline for scheduled maintenance from 8:00 to 11:00 a.m. tomorrow. I confirmed the maintenance window with the vendor today, but the vendor notice hasn't been attached to the remote-day draft yet. Since the draft plan schedules instruction through the LMS beginning at 8:00 a.m., we need to adjust immediately. Instructional files must be distributed by email as downloadable PDFs and made available for printing by 7:30 a.m. This also ties directly into Ms. Green's concern — those 38 households without reliable internet will need those printed packets ready at the same time.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Dr. Lee, I need to flag a critical transportation issue. My department's storm route review, completed this afternoon, found that no buses can safely travel tomorrow. This means we cannot send meals by regular bus routes as the draft plan currently assumes. Instead, meals should be made available for on-site pickup at North Campus and South Campus from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. These route review results have not yet been added to the operations briefing packet, so the draft plan still reflects the old bus-route meal delivery approach.

transcript.text: Dr. Lee, I need to flag a critical health support issue in the draft plan. The draft currently directs health questions to the usual school voicemail, but our district nurse coverage plan requires that voicemail be replaced entirely by a staffed nurse hotline from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. tomorrow for students who need medication or urgent health guidance during remote instruction. Voicemail is not to be used as a fallback or co-equal channel during this window. I confirmed the coverage roster this afternoon, but it has not yet been entered in the plan.
